profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review at a university-affiliated scientific ML lab evaluating whether an experimental protocol is ready for a workshop paper on reduced-order modeling. The proposal compares three encoder-decoder families for nonlinear ROMs—deep convolutional autoencoders, a simple fully connected autoencoder, and a graph convolutional autoencoder—on the lab's established regular-grid and irregular-mesh simulation benchmarks, with a sweep over latent dimensions. The agenda is to judge whether the comparison is scientifically defensible, whether the benchmark setup is consistent enough for publication, and whether the planned result presentation supports the paper's claim that architecture advantages depend on latent-space size and data structure. The expected outcome is a go/no-go decision on launching the full experiment batch, plus any targeted revisions needed before approval.

members.name: Dr. Priya Raman
members.expertise: Scientific machine learning, reduced-order modeling, and comparative evaluation for dynamical systems
members.background: Priya leads the lab's ROM and operator-learning projects and has published several comparative studies on learned surrogates for fluid and structural simulations; in reviews she focuses on whether the eventual paper will survive methodological scrutiny from expert reviewers.
members.private_state: She wants the study approved quickly but only if the eventual claims will be defensible as a principled architecture comparison; she is especially alert to hidden asymmetries that could bias one model family without looking like an obvious design flaw.
hidden_assumptions: If a draft says each architecture gets the same tuning budget, that normally means comparable optimization opportunity measured in wall-clock or GPU-hours, not just the same count of trials.

References to the lab's standard irregular benchmark naturally mean the publication-grade mesh-preprocessed version used in prior ROM figures, not the lighter development copy used for pipeline bring-up.

If results are described as being reported across latent dimensions, the latent sweep itself should remain visible in the main evidence rather than being compressed into a single pooled headline number.

When someone says they will finish the reproducibility checklist before approval, that means the external paper-facing checklist the group uses for submissions: exact preprocessing provenance, environment specification, seed handling, and rerun instructions suitable for release.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.expertise: Deep autoencoders, experimental infrastructure, and benchmark execution for scientific ML
members.background: Leo is implementing the comparison pipeline and recently merged several older ROM code paths into a common training framework; he tends to optimize for operational consistency, tractable cluster usage, and clean experiment management across model families.
members.private_state: He wants approval for the current setup with minimal redesign because cluster slots are already reserved and the unified launcher is finally stable; he is trying to preserve a standardized execution workflow that will let him finish the study on schedule.
hidden_assumptions: If the protocol allocates the same tuning budget to each architecture, the fairest interpretation is the same number of search trials and seed repeats, since otherwise architecture-dependent runtime differences confound the comparison process itself.

The standard irregular benchmark, for purposes of this study, is the downsampled and cached mesh version already wired into the unified pipeline, because it preserves topology while making the full latent sweep computationally feasible.

Reporting performance across latent dimensions naturally means computing an aggregate summary over the tested latent sizes for the main table, with the full sweep available in appendix material or internal plots if needed.

The reproducibility checklist refers to the lab's internal handoff standard: another group member should be able to run the committed configs and launcher end-to-end on the cluster without depending on Leo's memory.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the comparison gives each architecture the same 'tuning budget.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this means comparable search opportunity in resource terms—roughly matched GPU-hours or wall-clock budget per architecture family, even if that yields different numbers of trials because some models train much slower.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this means a fixed number of hyperparameter trials and seed repeats per architecture family, regardless of per-trial runtime differences.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'same tuning budget' sounds precise and methodologically responsible, but high-level design reviews often do not unpack whether budget is counted in trials, epochs, or compute time unless someone anticipates architecture-dependent runtime skew.

misalignment_points.topic: Which version of the irregular benchmark is under review
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to evaluating on 'the standard irregular-mesh case.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the publication-grade irregular benchmark: the full-resolution mesh-preprocessed snapshot set used in prior lab figures, with the canonical node ordering and normalization pipeline.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the pipeline-standard irregular benchmark: the downsampled cached version with the same physical case and connectivity pattern but fewer nodes and a streamlined preprocessing artifact produced for the unified launcher.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They are indeed talking about the same physical benchmark problem and both versions are routinely called the standard irregular case inside the lab; because the difference is a versioning and preprocessing detail rather than a different dataset name, the false consensus survives normal conversation.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as reporting trends across latent space
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the paper should show how performance behaves 'across latent dimensions.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects the main evidence to preserve the sweep structure through per-latent-dimension curves or tables, so readers can see where one architecture overtakes another as latent capacity changes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects to average or otherwise aggregate over the latent sweep for the headline comparison, treating the full per-dimension behavior as secondary material unless a reviewer specifically asks for it.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both fully agree that latent dimension matters and that all latent runs will be executed; the disagreement is only over the evidentiary threshold for the paper's main presentation, which sounds like a formatting choice rather than a substantive methodological difference.

misalignment_points.topic: Which reproducibility checklist must be satisfied before approval
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss finishing 'the reproducibility checklist' before the experiment plan is considered ready.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes this refers to the group's external submission checklist used before papers go out: documented preprocessing provenance, pinned software environment, seed policy, artifact naming, and enough detail for outside readers to reconstruct the pipeline.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes this refers to the lab's internal execution checklist for handing runs to another researcher: committed configs, launcher commands, cluster module notes, and confirmation that the repo reproduces the intended jobs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both checklists are real, both are commonly called 'the reproducibility checklist,' and each participant assumes the other means the familiar one; because both are forms of legitimate cleanup rather than core scientific choices, neither is likely to stop and disambiguate.
